reviewPolicy: GM Core curses are reviewed as trigger-driven single-effect afflictions. Only curses whose complete post-trigger mechanics are faithfully represented by Affliction Forge 0.1.55 ship as full. External world triggers are not engine blockers: applying a curse template represents that trigger having occurred. One-off narrative, inventory, body-part, third-party AI, rest-system, proficiency, or source-relative weakness rules do not justify bespoke Affliction Forge subsystems and remain inventory-only until a reusable contract exists or are later published as explicit manual-exception templates.

notes: Requires changing the rest duration needed to avoid fatigued while also suppressing rest and long-term-rest benefits but allowing daily preparations.
The affected skill is selected dynamically by the first trained-or-better skill check made after the curse takes hold.
Requires a Will save before identification, Recall Knowledge, or other interactions that depend on perceiving a creature's true form.
At turn start while frightened, the victim chooses fleeing or immobilized until end of turn.
The weekly repeat save is representable, but the core effect is integration with the starvation rules rather than an Affliction-stage effect.
The curse deals 5d6 damage matching the damage type used against the protected book. Repairing the book is a manual cure condition and is not itself an engine blocker.
Breaking any tracked promise deals 3d6 slashing damage that cannot be healed while the curse remains.
Each combat initiative roll triggers a new save; failure causes confused for 1 round as an incapacitation effect.
Failure sleeps for 1 round, critical failure sleeps indefinitely, and damage grants a new save against the curse.

The geographical trigger remains world/GM context. Applying the template represents entering the cursed area after the trigger occurs. Failure applies doomed 1; critical failure applies doomed 2 until the curse is removed.
Dying while cursed transforms the victim into a ghost or other incorporeal undead.
The daily repeat save is representable, but the core effect is integration with the thirst/dehydration rules.
Every animal that becomes aware of the cursed creature must save and may become hostile until death.
A theft removes a more valuable carried possession, or otherwise removes a limb and deals unhealable slashing damage until restitution.
Weakness 10 applies only to damage caused by worshippers of the deity that imposed the curse.
The curse DC scales from the curse level; nightly and burial-ground flat checks create temporary undead harassment. Returning the stolen goods is a manual cure condition.
